pages.title: Getting started
pages.description: Install PdfPecker and convert your first HTML to PDF in .NET, with the system requirements.

pages.title: HTML to PDF in C#
pages.description: How to convert HTML to PDF in C# and ASP.NET Core with PdfPecker: invoices from templates, headers and footers, fonts and images.

pages.title: Options
pages.description: PdfOptions: page size, margins, headers and footers, document properties, file access and limits.

pages.title: HTML and CSS
pages.description: The HTML elements, CSS selectors and properties, SVG and image formats PdfPecker supports.

pages.title: Paged media
pages.description: @page rules, margin boxes, named pages, running headers and tables of contents with page numbers.

pages.title: Markdown
pages.description: Convert CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown to PDF or HTML.

pages.title: Fluent C# API
pages.description: PdfPecker.Fluent: build PDFs from C# code in the style of QuestPDF, rendered by PdfPecker with no browser or native binaries.

pages.title: Images to PDF
pages.description: Put PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP or TIFF images into a PDF, one per page, at their own size or fitted to a page.

pages.title: Fonts
pages.description: Register TrueType, OpenType, WOFF and WOFF2 fonts, use @font-face, and handle missing fonts.

pages.title: Right-to-left, CJK and hyphenation
pages.description: Arabic and Hebrew text with bidi and shaping, Chinese, Japanese and Korean line breaking, and automatic hyphenation.

pages.title: PDF/A, passwords and watermarks
pages.description: PDF/A-2, 3 and 4 for archiving, AES-256 passwords and permissions, and watermarks.

pages.title: Accessibility
pages.description: Tagged PDF, PDF/UA-1 and PDF/UA-2 built from your HTML.

pages.title: Fillable forms
pages.description: HTML inputs, check boxes, radio buttons, selects and text areas as fillable PDF form fields, and filling and flattening the forms of existing PDFs.

pages.title: Digital signatures
pages.description: Sign PDFs with PAdES signatures, visible boxes, timestamps, existing fields and external signers, verify signatures, and add long-term validation data.

pages.title: E-invoices
pages.description: Factur-X, ZUGFeRD, XRechnung and Peppol invoice XML from invoice data, a ready-made invoice template, Factur-X PDF/A-3 e-invoices, and PDFs in UBL invoices.

pages.title: Barcodes
pages.description: QR codes, EPC payment QR codes (GiroCode), Code 128 and EAN-13 barcodes as vector SVG for your templates.

pages.title: Attachments
pages.description: Embed files in a PDF, read them back, or attach them to an existing PDF.

pages.title: Merging and splitting
pages.description: Merge any PDFs, stream them as they arrive, and extract, reorder, rotate and split pages.

pages.title: Stamping
pages.description: Put a stamp over or letterhead under the pages of any PDF.

pages.title: Compacting
pages.description: Make any PDF smaller, losslessly or with images downsampled and recompressed, keeping bookmarks, forms, tags and PDF/A.

pages.title: Text extraction
pages.description: Extract the text of any PDF in reading order with the position of every line and word, its images and its document properties.

pages.title: PDF to image
pages.description: Render PDF pages to PNG, JPEG, WebP or TIFF with PdfPecker's own renderer, or HTML straight to images.

pages.title: PDF to HTML
pages.description: Turn any PDF into one self-contained HTML page: page images with selectable, searchable text and working links.

pages.title: From wkhtmltopdf
pages.description: A wkhtmltopdf alternative for .NET: replace DinkToPdf, Rotativa or the wkhtmltopdf command line with PdfPecker, option by option.

pages.title: From HtmlRenderer.PdfSharp
pages.description: An HtmlRenderer.PdfSharp alternative now that PDFsharp 6.5 is AGPL: MIT-licensed, managed HTML to PDF with modern CSS.

pages.title: From IronPDF
pages.description: A free, MIT-licensed IronPDF alternative without Chrome: replace ChromePdfRenderer with PdfPecker and match its output.

pages.title: From PuppeteerSharp or Playwright
pages.description: Make PDFs from HTML in .NET without Chrome: replace PuppeteerSharp or Playwright page.pdf() with PdfPecker.

pages.title: Limitations
pages.description: What PdfPecker does not support yet, and what it leaves out by design.

pages.title: CSS support
pages.description: Every CSS property, at-rule, selector and unit, marked as supported, partly supported, missing or without effect on paper in PdfPecker.

pages.title: PDF feature checklist
pages.description: Every PDF feature, from encryption and signatures to layers and PDF/X, marked as supported, partly supported or missing in PdfPecker.

pages.title: Performance
pages.description: PdfPecker's speed and memory compared with Chromium, wkhtmltopdf, iText and other .NET converters.

pages.title: How it works
pages.description: PdfPecker's pipeline from HTML parsing through CSS and layout to the PDF writer and renderer.
